title: Severe bleeding
tldr: Call emergency services and press firmly directly on the bleeding wound with a dressing or clean cloth. Maintain pressure. For life-threatening bleeding from an arm or leg, use a commercial tourniquet if trained; follow dispatcher instructions.
steps: Check scene safety, use gloves if available and get emergency help.
Press firmly over the wound and keep pressing until bleeding stops or appropriate help takes over.
Use a tourniquet or wound packing for the appropriate injury if trained, following the device and dispatcher instructions.
Keep them from getting cold, check breathing and remain until responders arrive.
next: Get urgent medical assessment even if bleeding stops. Take a practical bleeding-control course.
watch: Do not pull an embedded object out; press around it and get help.
review_status: source-linked editorial review; not independent expert certification
without_help: Maintain firm pressure and have another person arrange the safest reachable medical care. A tourniquet, if indicated and used, must stay in place until a medical professional takes over; note its application time. Do not keep releasing pressure to check whether bleeding has stopped.
household: Give someone the specific task of calling or locating care while another person provides first aid. Keep the patient warm or cool as the condition requires and record what happened and when. Do not put yourself into the same hazard or assume an ambulance has been dispatched until confirmed. For this situation, brief every person on the first action: protect and call. Agree who will manage children, pets or mobility needs while that action happens. Do not pull an embedded object out; press around it and get help.
pack_now: For severe bleeding, prioritize only items needed for the first action and the fallback: Maintain firm pressure and have another person arrange the safest reachable medical care. A tourniquet, if indicated and used, must stay in place until a medical professional takes over; note its application time. Do not keep releasing pressure to check whether bleeding has stopped. Keep the relevant checklist and contact information within reach. Equipment retrieval must not delay the protective step.
scope: Civilian educational guidance. Linked references may use U.S. emergency systems; local warning methods, laws, services and conditions differ.
